Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:10:1.hebrew: כסף קבלת רבו - שמקבל רבו הכסף גרמו לו להשתחרר מאליו, ואין אחרים הללו חבין, אלא קבלת הרב. והרב אין נעשה שלוחו, אלא לצורך עצמו, ומקנהו מאליו. אבל חירות השטר — קבלת אחרים גרמה לו; וכיון דחוב הוא לו, אין חבין לאדם שלא מדעתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:10:1.english: [With regard to] money, his master’s receipt - That his master receives the money causes him to be emancipated automatically, and these other [people] are not acting to [his] disadvantage; rather, [it is] the master’s receipt [that effects it]. And the master does not become his agent, but rather [acts] for his own sake, and transfers him [to himself] on his own. But [with regard to] emancipation [by] a document, receipt by others caused it for him; and since it is a disadvantage for him, one cannot act to a person’s disadvantage without his consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:11:1.english: We heard them, etc. - In Tractate Gittin (daf 11b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:11:2.english: We learned - Like: "Did we not learn in the Mishnah?"

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:12:1.hebrew: דיש קנין - כי יהבי ליה ע"מ שאין לרבו רשות בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:12:1.english: That [a slave] has acquisition - When [someone] gives to him on condition that his master has no rights to it:

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:12:2.hebrew: והא קי"ל - כלומר, והא מעשים בכל יום שהעבד מקבל את גיטו. ואי רבנן פליגי עלה דמילתא, מי שבקינן רבנן ועבדינן כר"מ?:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:12:2.english: And yet we maintain - That is to say, behold, it is a daily occurrence that a slave receives his bill [of manumission]; and if the Rabbis disagree on this matter, would we abandon the Rabbis and act in accordance with Rabbi Meir?

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:13:1.hebrew: אף ע"י אחרים - ואפי' שלא מדעתו, דזכות הוא לעבד כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:13:1.english: Even through others - And even without his knowledge, for it is a benefit for a slave, etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:14:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון בן אלעזר היא - הך סיפא דשטר, דלית ליה גיטו וידו באין כאחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:14:1.english: And it is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar - [This refers to] this latter clause [concerning] a bill [of manumission], for he does not hold [that] his bill [of manumission] and his hand come simultaneously.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:14:2.hebrew: ושלש מחלוקות בדבר - רבי מאיר אית ליה: בכסף — על ידי אחרים, ואפי' שלא מדעתו, ולא ע"י עצמו, דאין קנין לעבד בלא רבו; ובשטר — ע"י עצמו, ולא ע"י אחרים שלא מדעתו, דחוב הוא לו; וכסף, אע"ג דחוב הוא לו, קבלת רבו גרמה לו. ור"ש בן אלעזר אית ליה: בין בכסף בין בשטר — ע"י אחרים, דקסבר זכות הוא לו, ולא ע"י עצמו; דגבי כסף אית ליה אין קנין לעבד בלא רבו, וגבי שטר לית ליה גיטו וידו באין כאחד, כדקתני ״אף בשטר כו'״, וכ"ש בכסף, אלמא בתרוייהו אית ליה ע"י עצמו לא. ורבנן דמתני' אית להו: בכסף — בין ע"י אחרים בין ע"י עצמו, דיש קנין, ועל ידי אחרים — דזכות הוא לו; וכן בשטר — בין ע"י אחרים בין ע"י עצמו. ודקיימא לן גיטו וידו באין כאחד — כרבנן עבדינן ליה. והאי דלא ערבינהו ותנינהו — משום דסיפא ר"ש בן אלעזר היא; אבל רישא, ה"ק ליה רבנן לר"מ: אף בכסף ע"י עצמו, דיש קנין, וכ"ש ע"י אחרים דזכות לו, וכ"ש שטר דזכות. ואם באנו לפרש ״שלש מחלוקות״, ולומר דרבנן אית להו בכסף בין ע"י עצמו בין ע"י אחרים, ובשטר — ע"י אחרים ולא ע"י עצמו, ורבי שמעון בן אלעזר סבר כר' מאיר בכסף, דע"י עצמו לא ואין קנין, וכרבנן בשטר, דאין גיטו וידו באין כאחד — א"כ, הא דקי"ל גיטו וידו באין כאחד, יחידאה היא, וכר' מאיר עבדינן ליה?! הילכך ליכא לפרושי אלא כדפרישית: דרישא דמילתא אמרוה רבנן, וסיפא אתאן לר' שמעון בן אלעזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:14:2.english: And [there are] three disputes with regard to the matter - Rabbi Meir maintains: With money, [emancipation can be effected] via others, and even without his consent, but not by himself, because a slave has no acquisition without his master; and with a bill [of manumission, it can be effected] by himself, but not via others without his consent, because [freedom] is a disadvantage to him; and regarding money, even though [freedom] is a disadvantage to him, the acceptance [of the money] by his master effects it for him. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar maintains: Both with money and with a bill [of manumission, it can be effected] via others, because he holds [that freedom] is an advantage to him, but not by himself; for regarding money, he maintains [that] a slave has no acquisition without his master, and regarding a bill [of manumission], he does not maintain [that] his bill [of manumission] and his hand come simultaneously, as it is taught: “Even with a bill [of manumission etc.]”, and all the more so with money; thus in both cases he maintains [that] by himself, [it is] not [effective]. And the Rabbis of our Mishnah maintain: With money, [it can be effected] both via others and by himself — [by himself,] because [a slave] can have an acquisition, and [via] others, because it is an advantage to him; and likewise with a bill [of manumission], both via others and by himself. And that which is established for us that “his bill [of manumission] and his hand come simultaneously” — we act in accordance with the Rabbis. And as for this [fact] that [the Mishnah] did not combine them and teach them [together] — [this is] because the latter clause is [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar; but in the first clause, this is what the Rabbis are saying to Rabbi Meir: Even with money by himself, because [a slave] can have an acquisition, and all the more so via others, since it is an advantage to him, and all the more so [with] a bill [of manumission], since it is an advantage. And if we were to interpret “three disputes” by saying that the Rabbis maintain [that] with money, [it can be effected] both by himself and via others, and with a bill [of manumission], via others but not by himself, and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds like Rabbi Meir regarding money, that by himself [it is] not [effective] and [a slave] has no acquisition, and like the Rabbis regarding a bill [of manumission], that his bill [of manumission] and his hand do not come simultaneously — if so, that which is established for us that “his bill [of manumission] and his hand come simultaneously” is [merely the opinion of] an individual [sage], and would we act in accordance with Rabbi Meir?! Therefore, it cannot be interpreted other than as I explained: that the first clause of the statement was stated by the Rabbis, and the latter clause brings us to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:15:1.hebrew: שאינה שלו - דכתיב (דברים כ״ד:א׳) ונתן בידה, ואיהי לא אקניה לבעל לגופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:15:1.english: That is not his - As it is written: “And he gives [it] into her hand” (Deuteronomy 24:1), and she did not transfer [ownership of] her person to the husband.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:15:2.hebrew: שאינה שלו - של רבו. ורבנן גמרי הכי: מה אשה מקבלת גיטה, אף עבד מקבל גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:15:2.english: That is not his - Of his master. And the Rabbis derive thus: Just as a woman receives her bill of divorce, so too a slave receives a bill of manumission.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי קטן הוה - ואעפ"כ הוצרך לכל זאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:1.english: And there are those who say he was a minor - And even so, [Mar Zutra] needed all this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:2.hebrew: ודלא כאבא שאול - דאמר: "כל המחזיק בהן זכה" — אפי' לאחר זמן זכה בהן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:2.english: And not in accordance with Abba Shaul - For he said: "Anyone who takes possession of them acquires them" — even after [some] time, he acquires them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:3.hebrew: ותנינא אין חבין לאדם כו' - אין אדם יכול ליעשות שלוחו שלא מדעתו לדבר שהוא חובה או הפסד, והיכי תני מתניתין דנפדה על ידי אחרים שלא מדעתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:2:3.english: And we learned: One cannot act against a person’s interest, etc. - A person cannot become his agent without his consent for a matter that is a disadvantage or a loss, and how [then] does the Mishnah teach that he is redeemed by others without his consent?

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:1.hebrew: ע"י עצמו לא - שאם נתן לו כסף לפדות את עצמו, אינו פדוי, דמה שקנה עבד קנה רבו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:1.english: Not by himself - That if [someone] gave him money to redeem himself, he is not redeemed, for whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:2.hebrew: במאי עסקינן - האי קנה עצמו ע"י אחרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:2.english: With what are we dealing - [Regarding] this [case where] he acquires himself by means of others.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:3.english: If we say without his consent - [That is, without the consent] of the slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:4.hebrew: שמעינן ליה לרבי מאיר - בפ"ק דגיטין. "חוב הוא לעבד שיוצא" כו' — שאם היה עבד כהן, פוסלו מן התרומה; ואי עבד ישראל, אוסרו בשפחה, דשכיחא ליה, פריצא ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:4.english: We have heard Rabbi Meir - In the first chapter of Gittin [11b]. [As for the statement,] "It is a disadvantage for a slave who goes out," etc. — for if he were the slave of a priest, [freedom] disqualifies him from [eating] terumah; and if [he were] the slave of an Israelite, [freedom] prohibits him from [cohabiting with] a maidservant, who is accessible to him [and] wanton with him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:5.english: We learned - Like "didn't we learn [in a mishna]":

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:6.hebrew: ותנינא אין חבין לאדם כו' - אין אדם יכול ליעשות שלוחו שלא מדעתו לדבר שהוא חובה או הפסד, והיכי תני מתניתין דנפדה על ידי אחרים שלא מדעתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:3:6.english: And we learned: One cannot act against a person’s [interest], etc. - A person cannot become his agent without his consent for a matter that is a disadvantage or a loss; and [if so,] how does the Mishnah teach that he is redeemed by others without his consent?

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:4:1.hebrew: אלא מדעתו - ואם תאמר: פשיטא! הא איצטריך לאשמועינן: דע"י עצמו — לא, דאין קנין לעבד בלא רבו בשום צד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:4:1.english: Rather, with his consent - And if you say: [Isn't it] obvious? This is what [the Mishnah] needed to teach us: that by himself, [it is] not [effective], for a slave has no acquisition without his master in any manner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:4:2.hebrew: ע"י עצמו לא - שאם נתן לו כסף לפדות את עצמו, אינו פדוי, דמה שקנה עבד קנה רבו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:4:2.english: By himself, no - For if [someone] gave him money to redeem himself, he is not redeemed, because whatever a slave acquires, his master acquires.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:5:1.hebrew: ואי מדעתו - שאמר לו: קבל גטי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:5:1.english: And if with his consent - That [the slave] said to him: "Accept my bill of manumission."

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:6:1.hebrew: באין כאחד - ולא אמרינן: לא הוציא רבו את הגט מרשותו, ואין זו קבלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:6:1.english: Come simultaneously - And we do not say [that] his master did not remove the bill [of manumission] from his possession, and [thus] this is not a [valid] receipt.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:6:2.english: But he did not teach - In the baraita like this:

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:8:1.hebrew: האי שטרא לחוד כו' - זה לשון קניה, וזה לשון שחרור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:8:1.english: This document is discrete, etc. - This [is the] language of acquisition, and that [is the] language of emancipation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:9:1.hebrew: האי כספא לחוד והאי כספא לחוד - זה ניתן לקניה, וזה ניתן לשחרור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:9:1.english: This money is discrete and this money is discrete - This is given for acquisition, and this is given for emancipation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 23a:9:2.english: In any event, the coin is one - And no difference is discernible between them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:14:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר אף שטר ע"י אחרים ולא ע"י עצמו ושלש מחלוקות בדבר - פירש בקונטרס: ר' מאיר אית ליה בכסף על ידי אחרים, ואפי' שלא מדעתו, ולא על ידי עצמו — דאין קנין לעבד בלא רבו; ובשטר — על ידי עצמו, ולא על ידי אחרים שלא מדעתו, דחוב הוא לו; וכסף, אע"ג דחוב הוא לו, קבלת רבו גרמה לו. ולר' שמעון בן אלעזר אית ליה בין כסף בין שטר על ידי אחרים, דקסבר זכות הוא לו; ולא ע"י עצמו — דגבי כסף אין קנין לעבד, וגבי שטר לית ליה גיטו וידו באין כאחד, כדקתני: "אף שטר" כו', וכל שכן כסף; אלמא בתרוייהו אית ליה ע"י עצמו לא. ורבנן דמתני' אית להו בכסף בין ע"י עצמו בין ע"י אחרים: ע"י עצמו — דיש קנין לעבד, ע"י אחרים — דזכות הוא לו; וכן שטר — בין ע"י עצמו בין ע"י אחרים. ודקי"ל דגיטו וידו באין כאחד — כרבנן עבידנא ליה. והאי דלא ערבינהו ותנינהו — משום דסיפא רבי שמעון בן אלעזר היא; אבל רישא הכי קאמרי ליה רבנן לר' מאיר: אף בכסף ע"י עצמו, דיש קנין לעבד, וכ"ש ע"י אחרים דזכות הוא לו, וכל שכן שטר. ואם באנו לפרש שלש מחלוקות ולומר: לרבנן אית להו בכסף בין ע"י אחרים בין על ידי עצמו, ובשטר ע"י אחרים ולא על ידי עצמו, ורבי שמעון סבר לה כר"מ דבכסף ע"י עצמו לא דאין קנין, וכרבנן בשטר דאין גיטו וידו באין כאחד — א"כ הא דקיימא לן דגיטו וידו באים כאחד יחידאה היא, וכר' מאיר עבדינן?! הילכך ליכא לפרושי אלא כדפרישית: דרישא דמילתא רבנן אמרוה, וסיפא אתאן לר' שמעון בן אלעזר. עכ"ל. וא"ת: מנא ליה הך שלש מחלוקות? דילמא כולה מילתא דרבנן דמתניתין — רשב"א, ובכסף ע"י עצמו היינו אף ע"י עצמו, ובשטר על ידי אחרים דוקא; והא דקיימא לן דגיטו וידו באים כאחד — משום דסבירא לן כרבי מאיר ולא כר"ש בן אלעזר? ויש לומר: אי גרסינן בברייתא דר' שמעון בן אלעזר "אף בשטר ע"י אחרים ולא ע"י עצמו", על כרחך יש שלש מחלוקות בדבר, דע"כ לאו היינו רבנן דמתני', דהא אמרי בהדיא בכסף על ידי עצמו; ולספרים דלא גרסינן "אף", צ"ל: כיון דאשכחן דרבנן פליגי עליה דרשב"א, כדאיתא בסוף פ"ק דגיטין (דף יב:) דאמרי "אי בעי זריק ליה גיטא ופסיל ליה", אלמא אית להו דגיטו וידו באין כאחד, וכיון דהכי הוא, לא קרי ליחיד "חכמים" במתניתין כיון דרבנן פליגי עליה; ולכך צריך לומר שיש שלש מחלוקות בדבר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:14:1.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Even [with] a document through others and not through himself, and there are three disputes regarding the matter - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Rabbi Meir holds [that emancipation] with money [can be effected] through others, and even without his consent, but not through himself, because a slave has no acquisition without his master; and with a document, [it can be effected] through himself, but not through others without his consent, because [emancipation] is a disadvantage for him; and [as for] money, even though it is a disadvantage for him, his master's acceptance [of the payment] caused it [to take effect]. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds [that] whether with money or with a document, [it can be effected] through others, for he maintains that it is an advantage for him; but not through himself, for regarding money a slave has no acquisition, and regarding a document he does not hold that his bill [of manumission] and his hand arrive simultaneously, as it teaches: "Even [with] a document, etc.", and all the more so with money — evidently in both of them he holds that [emancipation] through himself is not [valid]. And the Rabbis of our Mishnah hold [that emancipation] with money [can take effect] both through himself and through others — through himself because a slave has acquisition, [and] through others because it is an advantage for him; and similarly [with] a document, both through himself and through others. And that which we establish that his bill and his hand arrive simultaneously, we act in accordance with the Rabbis. And this that [the Mishnah] did not combine them and teach them [together is] because the concluding clause is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, but in the opening clause this is what the Rabbis were saying to Rabbi Meir: "Even with money [it can take effect] through himself, for a slave has acquisition, and all the more so through others because it is an advantage for him, and all the more so [with] a document." And if we were to explain [the] "three disputes" by saying that the Rabbis hold [that emancipation] with money [can be effected] both through others and through himself, and with a document through others but not through himself, and Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Meir that with money through himself is not [valid] because [a slave] has no acquisition, and like the Rabbis regarding a document that his bill and his hand do not arrive simultaneously — if so, that which we establish that his bill and his hand arrive simultaneously would be an individual opinion, and would we act in accordance with Rabbi Meir?! Therefore, it can only be explained as I explained: that the opening of the statement was said by the Rabbis, and the concluding clause brings us to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. Until here are his words. And if you say: From where does he [Rashi/the Gemara] know these three disputes? Perhaps the entire statement of the Rabbis of our Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, and "with money through himself" means even through himself, and "with a document through others" is specifically [through others], and that which we establish that his bill and his hand arrive simultaneously is because we hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir and not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar? And one can say: If we read in the baraita of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: "Even with a document through others and not through himself", perforce there are three disputes in the matter, for perforce this is not [the view of] the Rabbis of our Mishnah, as they explicitly said: "With money through himself"; and for the books that do not read "Even", one must say: Since we find that the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, as is found at the end of the first chapter of Gittin (12b), where they say: "If he wishes, he may throw him a bill [of manumission] and disqualify him [from eating terumah]", which proves that they hold that his bill and his hand arrive simultaneously; and since that is so, [the Mishnah] would not call an individual "the Sages" in our Mishnah when the Rabbis disagree with him; and therefore one must say that there are three disputes in the matter.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:2:1.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי קטן היה - ואעפ"כ הוצרך לזכות בו כדי שלא יקנה עצמו מן ההפקר אחר מיתת האדון, ודלא כאבא שאול — דלאבא שאול היה יכול לזכות בו ואפי' לאחר מיתה, כפ"ה. וקשה לר"ת: מנא ליה דלא כאבא שאול? דילמא לעולם אימא לך דכאבא שאול סבירא ליה, ומה שהחזיק בו מחיים — לפי שהיה ירא שמא יקדמנו אחר ויזכה בו! ועוד, ה"ל למימר: וכדרבנן! ועוד קשה: דבפרק השולח (גיטין דף לט.) פסיק רבי יהושע בן לוי הלכה כאבא שאול! ואע"ג דרבי יוחנן סבר דאין הלכה כאבא שאול, מ"מ קי"ל דבכל מקום הלכה כריב"ל לגבי דרבי יוחנן, כדמוכח בריש פ"ד דמגילה (דף כז.), דמשמע שדברי רבי יהושע בן לוי הם עיקר מדברי ר' יוחנן, גבי בית הכנסת מותר לעשותו בית המדרש; וא"כ, היכי עבוד הכא דלא כהילכתא? ונראה לר"ת דגרס הכא: וכאבא שאול — כלומר: אפילו לאבא שאול דאמר כל המחזיק בהן זכה בהן, הוצרך לעשות כן שלא יקדמנו אחר. ועוד מפרש ר"ת בענין אחר: איכא דאמרי קטן הוה — שאם היה גדול, לא היה מועיל בו זה פירש למיתה וזה פירש לחיים, ואע"פ שעבדות אחרים עליו, קודם הוא לזכות בעצמו, כיון שיש לו יד; אבל קטן שאין לו יד, כל הקודם זכה בהן, כאבא שאול. ולא אמר לו שלוף מסנאי מחיים, אלא לאחר מיתת יהודה הנדואה עשה כך, והיינו כאבא שאול דאמר: קטן אין לו יד לזכות בעצמו, ומשום הכי זכה בו מר זוטרא אפילו לאחר מיתה. אבל לרבנן, בין גדול ובין קטן, ואפילו עבדות אחרים עליו — קנה עצמו בן חורין. ור"י מפרש: דהא דקאמר וכאבא שאול, דאמילתא קמא נמי קאי, ואפי' ללישנא קמא דגדול הוה, לא היתה חזקה מועלת כלום אלא דוקא לאבא שאול; דלרבנן דאמרי: בין גדולים ובין קטנים קנו עצמן בני חורין, לא היה מר זוטרא יכול לזכות בו, דטעמייהו דרבנן מפרש בפרק השולח (גיטין דף לט:) דגמר לה לה מאשה: דמה אשה מיתת בעל מתירה בלא גט, אף עבד משתלח בלא גט, והוי השתא מיתת הבעל כגט, ואם היה נותן לו גט, מי היה אחר יכול לזכות בו?! אבל לאבא שאול ניחא, דהא יליף: מה אשה איסורה מפקעת במיתת הבעל ולא ממונא, אף עבד כו', וכיון שהיה משעבד עצמו למר זוטרא, לא היה חפץ לזכות בעצמו, והוי כמו קטן לאבא שאול:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:2:1.english: "And there are those who say he was a minor" - Even so, [Mar Zutra] needed to acquire him [during the master's lifetime] so that [the slave] would not acquire himself from the ownerless property after the master's death, and [this is] not in accordance with Abba Shaul — for according to Abba Shaul, he would have been able to acquire him even after [the master's] death, as the Kunteres explains. And Rabbeinu Tam raises a difficulty: From where does [the Gemara] know that this is not in accordance with Abba Shaul? Perhaps I could always say to you that he holds in accordance with Abba Shaul, and as for the fact that he took possession of him during [the master's] lifetime, that was because he was afraid lest another [person] precede him and acquire him! And furthermore, it should have said: "and in accordance with the Rabbis"! And furthermore, it is difficult: For in the chapter [entitled] HaSholei’ach (Gittin 39a), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi decided that the halakhah is in accordance with Abba Shaul! And even though Rabbi Yochanan holds that the halakhah is not in accordance with Abba Shaul, nevertheless we maintain that everywhere the halakhah follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi over Rabbi Yochanan, as is proven at the beginning of chapter 4 of Megillah (27a), which implies that the words of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi are primary over the words of Rabbi Yochanan regarding [the ruling that] a synagogue may be made into a study hall; and if so, how could they act here not in accordance with the halakhah? And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the reading here is: "and in accordance with Abba Shaul" — that is to say: even according to Abba Shaul, who said, "anyone who takes possession of them acquires them," he needed to do so lest another [person] precede him. And Rabbeinu Tam further explains in another manner: "There are those who say he was a minor" — for had he been an adult, [the mechanism of] "this one departed for death and that one departed for life" would not have been effective for him; and even though the servitude of others was upon him, he [the adult slave] is prior to acquire himself, since he possesses a "hand" [i.e., legal agency]. But a minor, who does not possess a "hand," whoever comes first acquires them, in accordance with Abba Shaul. And [according to this version], he did not say to him, "Remove my shoes," during [the master's] lifetime; rather, after the death of Yehuda the Indian he did so, and that is in accordance with Abba Shaul, who said that a minor does not possess a "hand" to acquire himself, and for this reason Mar Zutra acquired him even after death. But according to the Rabbis, whether an adult or a minor, and even if the servitude of others was upon him, he acquires himself as a freeman. And the Ri explains that this statement, "and in accordance with Abba Shaul," applies to the first matter as well; and even according to the first version, that he was an adult, the act of possession would not have been effective at all except specifically according to Abba Shaul. For according to the Rabbis, who say that both adults and minors acquire themselves as freemen, Mar Zutra would not have been able to acquire him. For the reason of the Rabbis is explained in the chapter [entitled] HaSholei’ach (Gittin 39b), that [they] derive [it via a verbal analogy of] "her" [lah] "her" [lah] from a woman: Just as [with] a woman, the death of the husband permits her without a bill of divorce, so too a slave is dismissed without a bill of emancipation; and the death of the master is now like a bill of emancipation, and had he given him a bill of emancipation, who else would be able to acquire him?! But according to Abba Shaul it is well, for he derives: Just as [with] a woman, [the husband's death] extricates her prohibition and not property, so too a slave, etc.; and since he was subordinating himself to Mar Zutra, he did not desire to acquire himself, and he is like a minor according to Abba Shaul.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:5:1.hebrew: [והא קמ"ל ע"י אחרים אין כו' - וא"ת: מעיקרא נמי ידע תלמודא דהכי הוא חידוש דמתניתין, כדאמר: בכסף ע"י אחרים אין, ע"י עצמו כו'? ויש לומר: דהוי סבר מעיקרא דהוי חידוש דמתני' מתרוייהו — ממה שהוא ע"י אחרים, ומן דיוקא דע"י עצמו לא; ומסיק דלא איצטריך מתני' אלא מן הדיוק. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 23a:5:1.english: ["And it teaches us this: By means of others, yes," etc. - And if you say: From the outset, the Talmud also knew that this is the novel teaching of the Mishnah, as it said: "With money [given] by others, yes; by [the slave] himself, [no]," etc.? And one can say: It thought initially that the novel teaching of the Mishnah was [derived] from both of them: from that which it is by means of others, and from the inference that by [the slave] himself, no; and it concludes that the Mishnah was needed only for the inference. — Tosafot Yeshanim]
